selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What did the traveller believe was the main purpose of life in this world?
questions.answer: He believed the main purpose of life is faith.

questions.question: How is the traveller described at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: He is described as someone who does not tire and is never satisfied with shallow searching.

questions.question: What careful step did he want to take before looking at the Qur'an’s teachings?
questions.answer: He wanted first to make sure it truly came from the Creator.

questions.question: How does the passage connect the Risale-i Nur to the Qur'an?
questions.answer: It presents it as a work that reflects the Qur'an’s light and explains its meanings.

questions.question: Before asking what the Qur'an teaches, what question did the traveller want answered?
questions.answer: He wanted to know whether it truly came from Allah.

questions.question: Why did the traveller begin with the Risale-i Nur instead of somewhere else?
questions.answer: Because he lived in this age and saw it as a present-day explanation of the Qur'an.

questions.question: Which two parts of the Risale-i Nur are said to show many ways the Qur'an is miraculous?
questions.answer: The Twenty-Fifth Word and the ending of the Nineteenth Letter.

questions.question: What does the failure of others to defeat the Risale-i Nur suggest about its source?
questions.answer: It suggests that its source is the Qur'an and that the Qur'an is divine speech.

questions.question: What happens to someone who truly sees that proof, according to the passage?
questions.answer: That person stops objecting and begins to admire the evidence.

questions.question: Who did the traveller speak to at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: He spoke to his own heart.

questions.question: Why did he want to examine the Qur'an?
questions.answer: Because it is said to be the speech of the One he was seeking.

questions.question: What was the traveller’s first source in this age for understanding the Qur'an?
questions.answer: His first source was the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Qur'an does to those who reject it?
questions.answer: It confronts them with a challenge in every age.

questions.question: What makes the Qur'an’s challenge unusual?
questions.answer: It continues across every age, not just one time.

questions.question: What does the passage say this strength of the Risale-i Nur shows about the Qur'an?
questions.answer: It shows that the Qur'an is its true source and authority, and that it is from heaven, not made by people.

questions.question: What is the Risale-i Nur trying to spread?
questions.answer: It is trying to spread the truths of the Qur'an everywhere.

questions.question: How many miraculous qualities are mentioned in that proof?
questions.answer: Forty are mentioned.

questions.question: How complete is the proof found there, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It is strong enough to show forty different sides of the Qur'an’s miraculous nature.

questions.question: What did the traveller say life is really about?
questions.answer: He said life is really about faith.

questions.question: What had to be settled first before studying the Qur'an’s message?
questions.answer: It had to be settled that the Qur'an is from the Creator.

questions.question: What made the Qur'an important enough for him to examine?
questions.answer: It was believed to be the word of the One he was seeking and to be the greatest and wisest book.

questions.question: How is the Qur'an presented in the passage compared with other books?
questions.answer: It is presented as the most famous, radiant, and wise book.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do the Twenty-Fifth Word and the end of the Nineteenth Letter help prove?
questions.answer: They help prove that the Qur'an has many miraculous qualities.

questions.question: What two sections are singled out as especially proving the Qur'an’s extraordinary nature?
questions.answer: The Twenty-Fifth Word and the ending of the Nineteenth Letter.
